limitations: RLIMIT_DATA applies to the kernel data_vm class: writable private mappings outside grow-down stacks. It is not a bound on shared, read-only, executable or grow-down stack mappings, kernel/page-table ownership, or complete RSS. Permission downgrades can leave resident pages outside this class.

Startup observations require other owners to remain quiescent during admission. The hard process data limit is not restored, including after failure. Kernel ignore_rlimit_data must remain disabled and observable throughout the worker lifetime. This qualification pins Linux 7.2.9-2-cachyos; other kernels/backends remain unqualified.

The separate Rust request ceiling bounds SpillAlloc-to-System request reservations, including in-flight requests and allocator headers. It excludes System usable-size rounding, metadata, fragmentation/retention, foreign allocations and direct mappings; it is not a complete allocator or RSS bound.
A refusal returns null through GlobalAlloc or failure through fallible reservations. Infallible Rust callers may abort; worker reservations still require physical exit before release/retry.

The cap is installed before Rayon and GPU initialization and cannot be relaxed or removed. Earlier bootstrap work retains its existing component/startup admission; other entry points without this worker admission do not gain an active cap.

Request peaks include in-flight reservations and may include calls that later fail in System. Existing successful live/peak request diagnostics keep their prior semantics. Snapshots remain non-atomic observations.

Allocator overhead/growth outside these requests, other caller/driver threads, cached stacks and shared driver ownership still need complete overlapping lifetime admission. Ordinary incomplete-profile admission remains closed.

All maintained proving families/routes, broader/live-cache workloads, five matched throughput pairs, 24 hours AND 150 roots, full-64/deadline/depth/size gates, multiple GPUs, AMD/Metal and newer Apple source integration remain open.
